title: Halting bound for the loop host
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and choose a Boolean mode. For any input word $x$, any configuration $c$ of $B$ on $x$ with no current state, any Boolean word $w$, and any configuration $f$ of $F$ on $x$, there is a time $t \le 2|u|+3$, where $u$ is the output word of $c$, such that the loop host built from $B$, $F$, $a$, and the chosen mode, started from the configuration formed using $c$, the empty prefix and initial output, the flag set to true, $w$, and $f$, has halted and has output $u$ in find mode and the one-letter word $[\mathrm{true}]$ otherwise.
